coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Nancy & Stephen Grand Family House
record.summary: The Nancy & Stephen Grand Family House is an 80-bedroom, ~92,000 sq ft nonprofit facility at 540 Mission Bay Blvd North (Mission Bay Block 7 East) providing free housing for families of children treated at UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital. DataSF Assessor records date its construction to 2016, matching UC San Francisco's own news office, which reported the building opened in May 2016.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed DataSF building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate; trimmed 117 sq m at the shared boundary with the neighboring Five88 parcel (blklot 8711226) -- see digitization_method.

open_questions: The UCSF News article could not be directly rendered in this session (its host returned 403 to automated fetches, and archive.org is blocked by this session's egress policy); its May 2016 opening date is taken from the article's own title/URL slug and is corroborated by independent secondary reporting (an SF Examiner 10-year-anniversary piece and a Hoodline article on the move), but the page's full text was not read firsthand here -- worth a follow-up direct read.
Exact day within May 2016 is not sourced, only the month.

A separate Family House article title found in search ('Grand Family House Grand Opening Ribbon Cutting... March 2, 2016') suggests a ribbon-cutting ceremony preceded the May 2016 move-in date, but that page returned 404 when fetched directly and its content could not be confirmed -- not used as a citation here.

record.notes: 5-story, 80-room nonprofit 'home away from home' for families of children being treated at UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital -- free lodging, low-income-qualified, run by the 501(c)(3) Family House, Inc. (founded 1981). Opened at this Mission Bay location in 2016 after moving from an earlier Judah St. building; accommodates up to 250 people/night, serves 3,000+ families/year. Assessor's welfare exemption on the parcel matches its nonprofit operation.
